title: Clear a left-in bearing off a shop bench can's spring screen, press-dip a second bearing, tray both, and close the lid
instruction: Put the bearing on the can's screen in the tray, press the other bearing down on the screen for a second, put it in the tray too, and close the can's lid.
context: The hard parts: the bearing left on the perforated dasher screen stands 9.2 mm above the can's rim, so the hinged lid physically strikes it and cannot close until that bearing is cleared; the second bearing must be held down at least 12 mm against the 18 N screen spring for at least 0.8 s before it springs back up; and the 0.98 kg steel can is light on the bench, so it slides or tips if the 172 deg overhanging lid is swung over without the other hand bracing the front handle, while closing the saucer lid requires releasing the rim past top dead centre and pressing from above so no finger is trapped. General maintenance and repair workers (1.5M US workers, O*NET 49-9071.00: 'Clean or lubricate shafts, bearings, gears, or other parts of machinery'), automotive mechanics (0.7M), and industrial machinery mechanics (0.41M) clean bearings on FM-approved spring-dasher bench cans (Eagle B-601) and close the cover immediately after use to contain solvent vapours (OSHA 1910.106).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench. Bench can: Eagle Manufacturing Model B-601 1-quart (0.95 L) 24-gauge galvanized steel safety bench can in red powder coat (model B601, UPC 48441223213, 15.88 cm OD x 9.21 cm closed height, 0.98 kg empty net weight, unpainted steel top retaining collar 11.8 cm ID, guided 11.4 cm perforated brass dasher screen resting 1.4 cm below the rim with 1.6 cm downward spring stroke, spot-welded 5.6 x 2.2 x 1.4 cm horizontal front strap handle, hinged 16.5 cm saucer cover opening 172 deg). Placed dry on yellow perimeter ticks at (26.5, 0.0) cm (within 2 mm), clocked within 3 deg so the lid hinge sits at 125 deg (open lid hanging toward (+y, -x) at 172 deg, ~4 cm off the bench) and the welded front strap handle sits at 215 deg facing the right arm. Bearings: two identical SKF 3305 A-2Z double-row shielded angular contact ball bearings (ISO 15: d = 25.0 mm, D = 62.0 mm, B = 25.4 mm, 0.35 kg each); one rests flat at the middle of the can's brass dasher screen (standing ~9.2 mm above the rim), and the second rests flat at the middle of a taped 12.0 x 12.0 x 0.3 cm black NBR rubber pad at (16.5, -20.5) cm (within 2 mm). Drain tray: Bochem Art. 8480 18/10 stainless steel instrument tray (20.0 x 17.5 x 1.5 cm, 0.24 kg) on yellow corner ticks at (35.5, -21.5) cm, 20.0 cm side along x (within 2 mm, 2 deg). Real trials run completely dry with no solvent in the can. Fixed layout: nothing varies by seed (--seed 0 gives trial seed 1415158438, same start).
scoring: 0 for good if at any step the can tilts past 12 deg or slides more than 30 mm from its yellow ticks, either bearing falls off the bench, or the tray shifts more than 25 mm or tilts past 10 deg (on the bench, judged from the trial video). Otherwise read at the end of the trial (dip depth and duration from the trial video). 0.0: lid left open above 4 deg (skirt-to-rim gap over 3.5 mm) or a bearing still in/on the can (idle = 0.0). 0.25: left-in bearing cleared off the can and lid closed within 4 deg (skirt-to-rim gap at most 3.5 mm all round). 0.5: 0.25 plus the second bearing pressed down on the dasher screen by at least 12 mm of its 16 mm stroke (puts the 25.4 mm bearing top at or below the 92.1 mm collar rim on video) for at least 0.8 s continuously (16 steps). 1.0: 0.5 plus both bearings resting flat and unstacked inside the 20.0 x 17.5 cm stainless tray, dasher screen sprung back up within 2 mm of its top stop, both hands at least 30 mm clear of the can, lid, tray and bearings, and all parts at rest (drift at most 3 mm, speeds under 10 mm/s and 0.10 rad/s) for 1.0 s (20 steps).
reset_notes: Between trials, about 40 seconds (dry can, no consumables): open the bench-can lid fully to its 172 deg rest, check the can and the Bochem 8480 tray sit on their yellow bench ticks within 2 mm and 2 deg, set one SKF 3305 A-2Z bearing flat at the middle of the brass dasher screen and the other flat at the middle of the black rubber pad within 2 mm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX; no liquid is simulated and real trials run dry. Can (16-stave hollow shell + collar + front strap handle, bench mu 0.25), saucer lid (hinge 0..172 deg, 0.22 N m dry friction), brass dasher (16 mm vertical slide, 1,125 N/m spring + 2.2 N preload = 18.0 N at 14 mm), tray and bearings collide at true 1:1 size: a bearing on the screen blocks the lid at ~23 deg ajar, and an unbraced lid pull slides the 0.98 kg can. Zero set_joint or write_pose in task or demo.
